stem: A complete list of all units belonging to a population, used as the basis for drawing a sample, is called a:

per_option_rationale.rationale: A sampling frame (or sample frame) is the complete list or enumeration of all units in the target population from which the sample will be drawn.
A census involves collecting data from every unit of the population; it is the process of complete enumeration, not the list used to draw a sample.
A parameter is a numerical characteristic (such as a mean or proportion) of the population, not a list of population units.
A statistic is a numerical characteristic computed from a sample; it is not a list of population units.

explanation: The sampling frame is the master list of all population units from which a sample is drawn. Without an accurate sampling frame, probability sampling cannot be carried out properly.

explanation_sections.punchline: The 'complete list of all units used as the basis for sampling' is the definition of a sampling frame.
explanation_sections.approach: State the property: sampling frame = complete enumeration of population units used to select the sample. Contrast: census = collecting data from all units (an activity); parameter = population numerical characteristic; statistic = sample numerical characteristic.
explanation_sections.lesson: The sampling frame is a prerequisite for probability sampling; its accuracy directly determines the quality of the sample.
explanation_sections.timing: 20 seconds by direct recall. Eliminate parameter and statistic (both are numbers, not lists) immediately.
